newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia moves on irrigation corporatisation.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia moves on irrigation corporatisation.

text.p: The state government of New South Wales (NSW) will commit more than A$100 million to upgrade assets to ensure a smooth transition to locally-managed irrigation schemes for the Murrumbidgee and Coleambally irrigation areas, NSW Treasurer Michael Egan said in a statement.
The government confirmed corporatisation of irrigation organisations would proceed.
Discussions with irrigation boards and agricultural associations were very positive, irrigation representatives said in the statement.

Creation of new state-owned corporations would convert management of important irrigation areas to a commercial structure, enabling them to be more competitive and environmentally sensitive, Egan said.

Creation of the new state-owned corporations would involve government commitment of more than A$100 million over the next 15 years to improve Coleambally and Murrumbidgee's assets, as well as creating competitive regionally-driven organisations, he said.
Cotton and rice are the main irrigated crops in NSW.
